newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS ACCUSER INSISTS SHE WAS RAPED, ATTORNEY SAYS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS ACCUSER INSISTS SHE WAS RAPED, ATTORNEY SAYS.

text.p: Attorneys for a woman who said she was sexually assaulted by Dallas Cowboys stars Michael Irvin and Erik Williams insisted Thursday that she was raped and denied police claims that she had admitted to lying.
Nina Shahravan, 23, turned herself in to police Thursday and was formally charged with perjury for allegedly inventing the rape allegations.

But her attorney G. David Smith told reporters Shahravan had not retracted her original rape allegations as police have reported, and that he intended to prove in court that she was assaulted at gunpoint.

"My client is the victim of a rape," Smith said. "I do not believe my client is guilty of the (perjury) offence. My client does not believe she is guilty of the offence, and we are going to fight this case vigorously."

Shahravan, a former topless dancer who has also worked at a mall makeup counter, posted a $500 bond Thursday and was released. She then made her way through a horde of photographers with a hood over her head.
It was the latest twist in a story which rocked the Dallas Cowboys on New Year's Eve, when Shahravan's allegations were first made public by police.
She accused Irvin of holding a gun against her head and threatening to kill her while Williams and a third man raped her on top of a pool table inside Williams' home Dec. 29.

Irvin and Williams, All-Pro stars seen as key to the Cowboys' success in recent years, emphatically denied the allegations from the start. Irvin said he had not been at Williams' home in 18 months and Williams also said he had done nothing wrong.
Dallas police concluded last Friday that Shahravan was lying and then filed perjury charges against her.
"Based on our investigation, Shahravan made malicious and false criminal allegations of sexual assault against three men," the Dallas Police Department said in a statement earlier this week.
Police sources said Shahravan had admitted to lying when confronted with the evidence. If convicted of the perjury charges, Shahravan could face up to one year in prison and a fine of $4,000.
But Smith said Shahravan's family also had hired a private investigator to prove she was raped.
